chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the 'ulī al-irbah' (those devoid of physical desire) from among the men. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The foolish slave who does not approach women.'

key_terms.أُولِي الْإِرْبَةِ: Those possessing the 'limb' (penis), often used to denote sexual potency or desire; here used to denote those devoid of it.
key_terms.الْمُوَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: The slave owned by someone (specifically the master).

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'ulī al-irbah' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Aban ibn Uthman clarifies that 'ulī al-irbah' refers specifically to a foolish slave who, due to his lack of sexual drive or impotence, does not approach women, thereby exempting him from the master's right to withhold his earnings for maintenance. This definition aligns with the juristic understanding that the term denotes a lack of physical capacity or desire rather than a voluntary abstinence, impacting the financial obligations of the master towards the slave. The hadith highlights the practical application of Quranic verses regarding slaves in marital contexts, emphasizing the master's authority over the slave's marital status based on his physical condition.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the ones from the men devoid of physical desire. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The stupid slave who does not go to the women’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of those among men who do not have the sense of carnal desires. He (the Imam) said, ‘They are the dimwitted ones who are owned and do not go near women.’”
